calls.prompt:
Company: Brightside Foods Co.

US mid-size packaged food company (~900 employees, plants in Ohio and Georgia). Makes hot dogs and sausages, brightly colored gummy candy, and pecan-and-apple snack bars. Buys pecans, apples and corn from US farms. Sells through grocery chains and convenience stores (many customers pay with SNAP / food stamps). Runs its own fleet of 40 delivery trucks. No restaurants, no alcohol, no exports.

Rules that APPLY:
- FDA food additive and color additive rules (dyes in candy, casings, meat)
- Food labeling and food safety rules for packaged food and meat products
- EPA pesticide residue limits on crops we buy (pecans, apples, corn)
- USDA marketing orders and grading for pecans and apples
- SNAP rules that change what shoppers can buy or who qualifies (affects demand)
- Workplace safety and labor rules for food plants; trucking safety rules for our fleet

Rules that DO NOT apply:
- Aviation, airspace, aircraft airworthiness
- Banking, securities, crypto, sanctions
- Medicare/Medicaid payment rules, medical devices
- Mining, offshore oil and gas, fisheries
- Broadcast/TV licensing

Affected areas and owners:
- food-safety: Additives, dyes, labeling, food safety → Maria Chen (Food Safety & Regulatory)
- sourcing: Ingredients from farms, pesticide limits, crop rules → Tom Alvarez (Sourcing)
- sales: Retail channels, SNAP, pricing → Aisha Grant (Sales Compliance)
- operations: Plant safety, labor, trucking fleet → Ben Kowalski (Operations)

Task: Find every US Federal Register document published between 2026-11-09 and 2026-11-13 (inclusive) that affects this company. For each, give the Federal Register document number, title, federalregister.gov URL, the key deadline, a tier (Critical if a deadline is < 90 days from 2026-11-13, otherwise High/Medium/Low by importance), the owner area, a one-line reason, and a one-line action. Only include items you found via search. Return an empty list if none.

items.reason: The requests include cancellation of a tioxazafen seed treatment registered for corn; the notice does not change residue tolerances. The comment deadline also applies to withdrawal requests.
items.action: Ask corn suppliers whether they use the listed treatment and track EPA’s final decision.

items.title: Revocation of the Color Additive Listing for Use of Orange B on Casings or Surfaces of Frankfurters and Sausages; Confirmation of Effective Date
items.reason: FDA confirmed that the authorization for Orange B on frankfurter and sausage casings or surfaces had already ended; there is no new deadline.
items.action: Verify immediately that current formulas, casing specifications, and supplier declarations show no Orange B use.

items.title: Pesticide Registration Maintenance Fee; Cancellation Order for Certain Pesticide Registrations
items.reason: The order cancels specific products, including a Glyfos registration labeled for corn, effective November 13, 2026, without changing crop residue limits; January 15, 2027 is the cutoff for registrants to sell or distribute existing stocks.
items.action: Cross-check growers’ pesticide registration numbers and confirm lawful existing-stock use or replacement plans.

items.title: Common Crop Insurance Regulations; Apple Crop Insurance Provisions; Withdrawal
items.reason: The proposal was withdrawn on November 13, 2026, leaving existing grower coverage rules unchanged by this action, with no filing deadline.
items.action: Remove the withdrawn proposal from the supplier-risk watchlist; no contract change is needed on this basis.

claimed.title: Pecans Grown in the States of Alabama, Arkansas, Arizona, California, Florida, Georgia, Kansas, Louisiana, Missouri, Mississippi, North Carolina, New Mexico, Oklahoma, South Carolina, and Texas; Changes to Membership and Handling Requirements
claimed.reason: USDA proposes changes to pecan handler transfer reports and late assessments, including for Georgia suppliers.
claimed.action: Confirm whether Brightside or its suppliers are covered handlers; assess reporting and cost impacts before deciding whether to comment.

claimed.title: Pioneer Hi-Bred International, Inc.: Availability of a Petition for a Determination of Nonregulated Status and Draft Plant Pest Risk Assessment for Insect Resistant COR-ØØ121-4 Maize (Zea mays)
claimed.reason: The petition could affect which corn varieties enter Brightside’s supply chain; it does not authorize the variety.
claimed.action: Check corn supplier specifications and any non-GE commitments; track the APHIS decision.

claimed.title: Pesticides; Notice of Receipt of Requests to Voluntarily Cancel Certain Pesticide Registrations and/or Amend Registrations To Terminate Certain Uses With a 30-Day Comment Period (June 2026)
claimed.reason: The requests include ending bearing-apple uses on two oxamyl registrations; the notice does not change residue tolerances. The comment deadline also applies to withdrawal requests.
claimed.action: Ask apple suppliers whether the listed registrations affect their pest-control program and whether they anticipate supply impacts.

claimed.title: Rules of Practice and Procedure for Administrative Hearings Before the Office of Administrative Law Judges
claimed.reason: The final rule generally requires represented parties to file electronically in covered DOL administrative proceedings.
claimed.action: Have labor counsel update filing and service procedures for any covered cases.

claimed.title: Agency Information Collection Activities: Requests for Comments; Clearance of a Renewed Approval of Information Collection(s): Procedures for Transportation Workplace Drug and Alcohol Testing Programs (ICR 2105-0529)
claimed.reason: DOT seeks to renew testing paperwork that covers regulated motor carriers; the proposed form edits do not add a fleet reporting duty.
claimed.action: Keep existing testing and reporting procedures in place; comment if the current paperwork creates a material burden.

claimed.title: Color Additive Petition From the International Association of Color Manufacturers; Request To Amend the Color Additive Regulations To Remove the Solvents Methylene Chloride, Trichloroethylene, and Ethylene Dichloride
claimed.reason: FDA removes authorizations for specified extraction solvents used to make annatto extract, paprika oleoresin, and turmeric oleoresin; objections or hearing requests are due December 10, 2026.
claimed.action: Identify affected color ingredients and obtain supplier confirmation that their extraction methods comply by the January 11, 2027 effective date.

claimed.title: Color Additive Petition From Environmental Defense Fund et al.; Request To Amend the Color Additive Regulations To Remove the Solvents Ethylene Dichloride, Methylene Chloride, and Trichloroethylene
claimed.reason: This separate FDA order removes the authorization for methylene chloride as a diluent in fruit and vegetable marking inks, potentially affecting marked apples; objections or hearing requests are due December 10, 2026, and the order takes effect January 11, 2027.
claimed.action: Ask apple suppliers whether they use direct marking inks and, if so, obtain updated specifications.

claimed.title: Modification to Work Requirements for Able-Bodied Adults
claimed.reason: Proposed SNAP time-limit, exception, and waiver changes could affect how many shoppers receive benefits.
claimed.action: Estimate demand exposure with grocery and convenience accounts that have high SNAP sales.

claimed.title: Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program: Reforming Categorical Eligibility
claimed.reason: USDA proposes narrowing the TANF pathway to categorical SNAP eligibility, which could reduce participation and retail demand.
claimed.action: Model sales exposure separately from the work-requirements proposal and decide whether to comment through a trade association.

claimed.title: Unemployment Insurance Program National Minimum Weekly Work Search Requirements
claimed.reason: The proposed federal minimum applies to state unemployment programs and claimants but could indirectly affect recruiting and laid-off employees.
claimed.action: Have HR assess implications for Ohio and Georgia hiring and layoff communications; no immediate procedure change is required.

claimed.action: Update counsel’s reference materials and calendar the 14-day response window if served with a covered petition.

perItem.why: Names Georgia suppliers and a concrete check, but terms like handler transfer reports and late assessments are jargon, and the action is somewhat generic.
Plain reason that the petition does not authorize the variety, a concrete supplier-spec check, and an owner who fits sourcing.
Concrete supplier question about pest-control impact, but bearing-apple uses, residue tolerances, and withdrawal requests need translation.
The owner is Operations while the action hands the work to labor counsel, and the reason relies on terms like represented parties and covered proceedings.
Clear that no new fleet reporting duty applies, but the action to keep procedures and comment if burdened is generic.
Specific to annatto, paprika, and turmeric ingredients with dates, and asks for a concrete supplier compliance confirmation before January 11, 2027.
Ties the marking-ink solvent ban specifically to marked apples, with a concrete ask to suppliers for ink specifications.
Links SNAP changes to specific grocery and convenience accounts with a concrete exposure-estimate step, though the reason is somewhat abstract.
Concrete modeling and trade-association steps, but categorical eligibility and TANF pathway are jargon for a non-lawyer.
Names Ohio and Georgia hiring as the exposure with a clear HR step, but the owner is Operations while the action goes to HR, and the reason is fairly generic.
Opaque title and reason about advisory-opinion procedures; the Operations owner is a poor fit for updating counsel's legal references.
Specific to the tioxazafen corn seed treatment with a concrete supplier question and a tracking step.
Specific Glyfos corn registration and January 15, 2027 cutoff with a concrete cross-check of grower registration numbers, though registrants and existing stocks are jargon.
Plain reason that the apple insurance proposal was withdrawn and no contract change is needed, with a concrete watchlist action.
